question: A product page uses `revalidate: 300`. It was generated at 10:00. The price changes at 10:01 and the next visit happens at 10:07. What does that visitor see?
options: The new price, because the page is older than 5 minutes
The old price, and the visit triggers a background regeneration; later visitors see the new price
A loading state while the page regenerates
The old price until the next deploy
explanation: Stale-while-revalidate: the first request after expiry receives the cached (stale) HTML instantly and starts the regeneration.

question: Why must a regeneration be deduplicated per path?
options: React cannot render the same page twice
So a popular page that expires does not start one render per concurrent request and overload the CMS or database
Because CDNs reject duplicate HTML
To keep the hydration bundle small
explanation: Hundreds of requests can hit an expired page in the same second. One shared regeneration avoids a thundering herd on the data source.

question: The CMS is down when a page tries to regenerate. What should an ISR server do?
options: Serve a 500 error until the CMS is back
Delete the page from the cache
Keep serving the last good HTML and try again on a later request
Fall back to client-side rendering for every visitor
explanation: A failed regeneration must not replace a working page. Visitors keep getting the last successful version.

question: Editors want published changes live within seconds, but renders are expensive and most pages change once a month. Which setup fits?
options: `revalidate: 1` on every page
SSR on every request
A long (or no) time window plus on-demand `revalidatePath`/`revalidateTag` from a CMS publish webhook
A full rebuild on every publish
explanation: On-demand revalidation refreshes exactly the affected pages when data changes, so the timer can be long and renders stay rare.

question: Which data should NOT rely on ISR alone?
options: A blog post body
The stock count shown on the checkout step
A product description
A category landing page
explanation: ISR pages can be stale for a whole window and are shared by every visitor. Data that must be exact at the moment of the decision is fetched per request.
